definition: Fact bargaining is a type of plea bargaining. It refers to an agreement between a prosecutor and a defendant over what version of the facts will be presented in court. Fact bargaining plays a major role in sentencing; indeed, certain facts can increase or decrease one’s sentence depending on the corresponding sentencing guidelines. For example, under three-strikes laws, a person who committed a severe violent felony and two other previous convictions will serve a mandatory life sentence in prison. It is particularly important for drug-related offenses as the amount of drugs carried by the defendant can change the sentence drastically.
